import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Dog Registration Analysis in Zurich, Switzerland', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# 1. Top 10 Dog Breeds
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
colors = sns.color_palette('viridis', 10)
bars1 = ax1.barh(top_breeds.index[::-1], top_breeds.values[::-1], color=colors)
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(top_breeds.values[::-1]):
    ax1.text(v + 50, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=9)

# 2. Dog Registration by District (Kreis)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
# Get the latest year data to avoid counting same dogs multiple times
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year]
district_counts = df_latest.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors2 = sns.color_palette('coolwarm', len(district_counts))
ax2.barh(district_counts.index, district_counts.values, color=colors2)
ax2.set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('District', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title(f'Dog Distribution by District ({latest_year})', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 3. Dog Age Distribution
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
age_order = df_latest.sort_values('AlterVHundSort')['AlterVHundLang'].unique()
age_counts = df_latest['AlterVHundLang'].value_counts().reindex(age_order).dropna()
colors3 = sns.color_palette('Blues', len(age_counts))
ax3.bar(range(len(age_counts)), age_counts.values, color=colors3)
ax3.set_xticks(range(len(age_counts)))
ax3.set_xticklabels(age_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax3.set_xlabel('Dog Age', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Dog Age Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Owner Age Group vs Dog Gender
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
# Create crosstab of owner age group and dog gender
owner_dog_cross = pd.crosstab(df_latest['AlterV10Lang'], df_latest['SexHundLang'])
owner_dog_cross = owner_dog_cross.reindex(df_latest.sort_values('AlterV10Sort')['AlterV10Lang'].unique())
owner_dog_cross = owner_dog_cross.dropna()

x = range(len(owner_dog_cross))
width = 0.35
if 'männlich' in owner_dog_cross.columns:
    bars_m = ax4.bar([i - width/2 for i in x], owner_dog_cross['männlich'], width, label='Male Dogs', color='steelblue')
if 'weiblich' in owner_dog_cross.columns:
    bars_f = ax4.bar([i + width/2 for i in x], owner_dog_cross['weiblich'], width, label='Female Dogs', color='coral')

ax4.set_xticks(x)
ax4.set_xticklabels(owner_dog_cross.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax4.set_xlabel('Owner Age Group', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Dog Gender Distribution by Owner Age Group', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend()

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
